To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the strategic management process of a firm is the process by which it sets strategic direction for the firm, formulates strategies to implement this direction, implements and monitors the strategies, and adjusts its strategic direction as a consequence of the monitoring process; (2) a firm's strategic direction is determined primarily by the needs and expectations of its stakeholders; (3) the firm's strategy is a set of decisions and actions that will enable it to achieve its strategic direction and satisfy the needs and expectations

1) the more a CEO is involved in the board’s work, the higher the firm’s performance (the CEO involvement effect); 2) the higher the CEO’s involvement, the lower the firm’s performance when the board is more involved in strategy and monitoring (the CEO involvement x board involvement effect); 3) the CEO’s involvement in the board’s monitoring activities has the largest impact on the firm’s performance.
